intro_html: A regular roll: nori on the outside, rice inside it, and in the middle long strips of tuna laid end to end with long slices of mango — nothing cubed or minced. It's rolled the way Just One Cookbook rolls her maki, but on a whole sheet of nori so there's room for both fillings and a line of her spicy mayo. Start with sushi rice at room temperature.

notes.html:
• JOC's tuna roll (tekka maki) is a thin roll: half a sheet of nori, 80 g of rice, one filling.
  • Tuna, mango and mayo need more room, so this doubles it — a whole sheet and 160 g of rice — for a medium roll (chumaki).
  • For a thin roll, go back to half a sheet with one tuna strip and one mango slice.

• A thin line inside, along the filling, so every piece gets some; a small dot on top for the look.
  • Too much inside makes the filling slide out — keep the line thin.

• Strips and slices that run the full length of the roll show up in every piece as a clean square of tuna and a stripe of mango.
  • Short gaps between strips are fine.
The mango, the mayo inside, the whole sheet (she uses half for tuna) and cutting into 8 (she cuts a thin roll into 6).

• Too much rice or filling, or rice spread over the bare strip.
  • Keep the rice airy, the filling to one neat row, and press gently.

• Buy tuna sold for raw eating and keep it cold until you roll.
  • Don't keep the rolls in the fridge for long: the rice goes hard.

steps.body_html:
• Stir together:
    • japanese mayonnaise (kewpie) 60 ml (¼ cup)
    • sriracha 1 tbsp
    • lime juice a splash
  • Spoon it into a small piping bag (or a zip bag with a tiny corner cut off) — it pipes a thin line inside the roll and a dot on top.

how.caption: Stir the mayo, sriracha and lime together.
Spoon it into a small piping bag.

steps.title: Spicy mayo

steps.body_html:
• Cut the block into slabs about 1 cm thick, then each slab into strips 1 cm wide — as long as the block allows.
  • Each cut is one long pull of the knife from heel to tip; don't saw.
  • You need enough strips to lie end to end across the nori (about 20 cm per roll).

how.caption: Cut the block into slabs about 1 cm thick.
Cut each slab into long 1 cm strips — one long pull of the knife from heel to tip, no sawing.

steps.title: Tuna into long strips

steps.body_html: Peel the mango, cut the two cheeks off the stone, and slice each cheek lengthwise into long slices about 7 mm thick.

how.caption: Peel the mango and cut the two cheeks off the stone.
Slice each cheek lengthwise into long slices about 7 mm thick.

steps.title: Mango into long slices

steps.body_html:
• Bamboo mat with the slats running sideways.
  • A whole sheet of nori on it, shiny side down, long side along the near edge of the mat, with 3–4 slats showing nearest you.

how.caption: Whole nori, shiny side down, long side along the near edge, 3–4 slats showing.

steps.title: Set up the mat

uses_rows.amount_html: 2 whole sheets

steps.body_html:
• Mix the tezu and wet your fingers in it.
  • Put 160 g of rice on the nori, left of centre, and spread it to the right and out to the edges with your fingertips.
  • Keep an inch (2.5 cm) of nori bare along the far edge — it seals the roll.
  • Spread, don't press: the rice should stay airy.

how.caption: Wet your fingers in the tezu.
Rice on left of centre, spread it right and out — an inch bare along the far edge.

steps.title: Spread the rice

uses_rows.amount_html: 240 ml (1 cup)

steps.body_html:
• Lay tuna strips end to end across the middle of the rice, so they reach both ends — add a short piece at the end if one is too short.
  • Lay mango slices right beside them, end to end.
  • Pipe a thin line of spicy mayo along the filling.

how.caption: Tuna strips end to end across the middle of the rice.
Mango slices right beside them, end to end.
Pipe a thin line of spicy mayo along the filling.

steps.title: Fill

steps.body_html:
• Hold the filling down with your fingertips.
  • Lift the near edge of the mat with your thumbs and, in one movement, roll the nori and rice over the filling so the near edge lands right on the far edge of the rice.
  • The inch of bare nori is still showing.

how.caption: Fingertips hold the filling down; thumbs lift the near edge of the mat.
In one movement, roll over the filling so the near edge lands on the far edge of the rice.

steps.title: Roll over the filling

steps.body_html: Leave the mat over the roll and gently shape and tighten it with your fingers from outside the mat — round, or with square sides.

how.caption: Leave the mat on and shape the roll with your fingers from outside it.

steps.title: Tighten through the mat

steps.body_html:
• Lift the mat and turn the roll once so the bare strip wraps over and seals it.
  • Squeeze gently through the mat once more. Leave it seam side down and make the second roll.

how.caption: Lift the mat and turn the roll once so the bare strip seals it.

steps.title: Seal

steps.body_html:
• Wet the knife on a damp cloth.
  • Cut the roll in half, each half in half, then each piece in half again — 8 pieces.
  • Push the knife forward, then pull it back through the roll; wet it again between cuts.

how.caption: Wet the knife on a damp cloth.
Push forward, then pull back — half, then quarters, then eighths.

steps.title: Cut into 8

steps.body_html:
• A small dot of spicy mayo on each piece.
  • Soy sauce and gari on the side; best eaten the same day.

how.caption: A small dot of spicy mayo on each piece.

steps.title: Serve

timeline.note_html: Keep the tuna in the fridge until you roll, and the rice under a damp towel.
